rationale.b: Ranking uses signals that connectors collect, but rendering and ranking are not connector functions.
rationale.a: Right. Connectors fetch data from connected applications and parse item content and permissions.
rationale.c: A connector integrates with the system where content lives. It does not host or back it up.
rationale.d: Answer generation happens downstream of the index, not in the connector.

rationale.a: Right. With no activity pushed, limited signals make ranking suboptimal, and results are more likely to be outranked by connectors with stronger signals.
rationale.b: Activity signals such as views, edits, and shares drive relevance ranking.
rationale.c: Activity affects ranking, not whether a permitted document can appear.
rationale.d: Upload times are not user activity. Nothing replaces pushed activity signals.

rationale.b: Native connectors are Glean's. Partner connectors are developed and supported by the partner.
rationale.c: The admin configures it, but the partner develops and supports the integration.
rationale.d: A listed partner connector is the partner's to maintain and support.
rationale.a: Right. Partner connectors use the Indexing API but are developed and supported by the partner, and Glean expects the partner to maintain a listed connector.

rationale.b: Use an existing connector before building a new one.
rationale.c: That is the web history connector, delivered through the Glean browser extension.
rationale.a: Right. Push API connectors suit custom applications, self-hosted environments, and systems behind firewalls.
rationale.d: Freshness-dominant data with actions calls for live tools or MCP.

rationale.b: Sensitivity is handled by mirrored permissions. Live access does not help historical, cross-document recall.
rationale.a: Right. Indexed mode suits bulk corpora and historical or cross-document questions.
rationale.c: A single request-time fetch cannot search three years of pages.
rationale.d: Web history shows page titles from a user's own browsing, not page content.

rationale.a: Right. Live retrieval suits data where freshness dominates or continuous full indexing is impractical.
rationale.c: Code is listed with the bulk corpora that suit indexing.

rationale.b: That describes live access, which can require each user to authenticate.
rationale.c: Indexing mirrors source permissions. A user who cannot access an item in the source should not see it in Glean.
rationale.d: The service account fetches data. Users see results according to the mirrored permissions.
rationale.a: Right. The source may still enforce access again when the user opens the item.

rationale.b: MCP servers do not crawl content into the index.
rationale.c: No such rule exists. The tickets were never indexed.
rationale.a: Right. Searchable content needs an indexing connector.
rationale.d: Custom Metadata attaches to documents that are already indexed. These tickets were never indexed.

rationale.b: The Indexing API configures push datasources, not MCP tools.
rationale.a: Right. Deployments created on or after September 22, 2026 use Connectors for catalog-backed MCP integrations.
rationale.c: Catalog MCP integrations need no custom connector.
rationale.d: That path is for custom or unlisted remote MCP servers, not catalog entries.

rationale.a: Right. NetSuite MCP uses each user's own credentials and role at request time and depends on the native NetSuite connector.
rationale.b: It depends on the native NetSuite connector being set up.
rationale.c: It provides real-time access at request time.
rationale.d: It is documented in Glean product documentation alongside the native NetSuite connector.

rationale.b: Row-level indexing of a data lake is exactly what the guidance steers away from.
rationale.c: Extrapolating from a sample gives wrong aggregate answers.
rationale.d: Web history returns page titles only, never the numbers.
rationale.a: Right. For large structured data lakes, the guidance is to query with a custom action or MCP server.

rationale.b: Implementation choices come after you decide a connector is justified.
rationale.a: Right. Scoping starts by checking for a native connector or web crawler option.
rationale.d: Hosting is chosen before you build, but only after fit is established.
